content.introduction: Investing in health care stocks can diversify your portfolio and benefit from industry growth. Health care is a major sector in the S&P 500. Consider stable companies and emerging fields like biotechnology.
body: * What is the health care sector? # Health care sector: Investing in stocks that help keep you well. Regardless of your age, condition, or financial situation, you likely spend some money on products and services to maintain your health, whether it’s a few bucks at the pharmacy or a major hospital visit. * Health care is prominent within the S&P 500; it’s one of the largest segments of the index’s 11 sectors. * Many health care industries are noncyclical, but some (like biotechnology) operate in emerging and speculative fields. Knowing which industries in the sector to invest in and when can help you position your portfolio for growth, mitigate market risk, and take advantage of both stable and speculative opportunities in the market. So if you’re thinking of adding health care stocks to your portfolio, get to know the industries and companies well, make sure they match your investment strategy, and pay attention to the regulatory and health-related trends affecting the sector.

Over 40% of adults in the U.S. and 16% globally are considered candidates for some form of weight loss support according to reports from the Center for Disease Control[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_ee96) and the World Health Organization,[3](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_8334) while heart disease remains the leading cause of death in the U.S.,[4](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_7c3) and cancer ranks second.[5](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_58b) Diabetes affects over 11% of the U.S. population,[6](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_f398) nearly half of U.S. adults have high blood pressure,[7](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_e1d) and mental health disorders affect millions of Americans annually,[8](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_e2c4) underscoring how many people rely on ongoing care and medication. McKinsey Company estimates that for every $10 billion in revenue, AI could help health insurers save between $150 million and $300 million in administrative costs, and up to $970 million in medical costs.[9](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/healthcare-stocks.html#footnote_region_b64) Those potential savings help explain why many investors watch AI adoption closely, while also recognizing that healthcare organizations must implement changes carefully and within strict oversight.
